proof: Each T contains4 unit squares and covers3 cells of one checkerboard parity and1 of the other. A full board tiling would use an odd number of Ts (5 or9); the total parity imbalance is twice a sum of an odd number of +1/-1 terms, hence nonzero. Both boards have equal black/white counts. So area upper bound5/9 is unattainable; explicit disjoint packing of4/8 proves maximum. Coordinates are proof-only, never added to displayed board.
